clue.text: Egyptian peninsula/desert island trail European retraced before mass opposition to elites

indicators.note: the reversed run is placed before the final piece in the answer
to retrace a path is to go back along it, so the whole string of pieces is read in reverse order

parts.note: Sinai is the peninsula (and desert) in north-east Egypt
to desert is to rat on someone
to trail behind is to lag
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A traveller retraces a route across Sinai and an island trail, all before some mass protest against the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retraced' turns the whole five-piece run backwards, not each piece. The slash makes 'desert' look like a second name for the peninsula, but it is a verb meaning betray.
explanation.definitionFit: Egalitarianism is the belief in equality for all, which sets it against privileged ruling groups.

clue.text: Goober's initiation at prison, sent up in US version of Porridge

indicators.note: the initiation of a word is its beginning, so only its opening letter is taken
in a down clue, sent up means the word is written bottom to top, read backwards

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A Southern inmate called Goober starts his sentence, a US take on the British sitcom Porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' reverses STIR to RITS. Porridge was a British TV sitcom set in a prison, and 'porridge' is also British slang for a prison term; the capital P is misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: Grits is coarsely ground maize boiled into a breakfast mush, the American Southern counterpart of oat porridge.

clue.text: How sad for fogeys to be 24 hours short

parts.note: to be short of something is to lack it
twenty-four hours makes a day

explanation.surface: Old-timers lament that a day never seems long enough for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for fogeys' marks the definition as an old-fashioned word; 'to be' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lackaday is an archaic exclamation of regret, the sort of word only old-timers would still use.

clue.text: Exercises in rotation can guarantee ultimately becoming thinner

indicators.note: the exercises are placed in the middle of the word for rotation

parts.note: a turn is a rotation
PE is physical education, school exercises
a tin is a can

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Doing exercises in turn is promised to make you slimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thinner' reads as slimmer but is a noun: a solvent that thins paint. 'becoming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpentine is a solvent used to dilute oil paint, i.e. a paint thinner.

clue.text: Guy possibly to drive away from outer place

indicators.note: the abbreviation for place is taken away from the outside of the word for drive

parts.note: to propel is to drive forward

explanation.surface: Someone is told to drive a guy away from a remote spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing P and L from the outside of PROPEL leaves ROPE. 'Guy' looks like a man but is a guy rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy is a rope or line used to steady a tent or mast, so it is one example of a cord.

clue.text: Site of sudden inflation, to be expected in crash

definitions.text: Site of sudden inflation, to be expected in crash

parts.words: Site of sudden inflation, to be expected in crash
parts.note: reads like an economics comment on prices ballooning before a market crash, but describes a car safety device that blows up on impact

explanation.surface: Economists expect a burst of price inflation followed by a market crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's safety cushion inflates instantly when a collision occurs, cushioning the occupant.

clue.text: Resentment about name as fake

indicators.note: the word for resentment goes about, or around, the other pieces

parts.note: ire is anger or resentment
as in the sense of because means since

explanation.surface: Someone is bitter that a name has been used falsely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is easy to pass over as a link word, but it supplies SINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone insincere is putting on feelings they do not have, i.e. false.

clue.text: Sudden loss of diversity revised in simian contexts

indicators.note: revised means altered and rewritten, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A study of primate habitats has been rewritten to show falling variety among apes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass extinction is when a large share of species die out in a short period, slashing biodiversity.

clue.text: Abandoning half of interrogations, headmaster has to ease off outside

indicators.note: the word for ease off goes outside, enclosing the other pieces

parts.note: to relent is to ease off

indicators.note: half of means only the first half of the word for interrogations is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: inquisitions are searching interrogations
HM is the abbreviation for headmaster

explanation.surface: A head teacher gives up half of his questioning and must go easier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps the first six letters of the synonym INQUISITIONS, which the solver must supply. 'outside' wraps the easing-off word round the rest; 'has to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Relinquishment is the act of giving something up, i.e. surrendering it.

clue.text: Old calculator turning tooth to output any number

indicators.note: to output something is to put it out, so a letter is removed
turning means the word for tooth is read backwards

parts.note: a canine is a pointed tooth
N stands for any number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A vintage calculating machine turns out any number of results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses CANINE to ENINAC; 'to output' then drops an N.
explanation.definitionFit: ENIAC was a pioneering 1940s electronic computer, an early machine for computation.

clue.text: Adjust sharp back of chair and see couches differently

indicators.note: to adjust something is to rearrange it, so the letters that follow are reshuffled
the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone tweaks a sharp chair back and sees the sofas in a new light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couches' reads as sofas but is a verb: to couch words is to express them. 'and' just links the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To couch an idea is to put it into words, so expressing it in other words is to reword it.

clue.text: Seriously wearing black suit

parts.note: to be in something is to be wearing it
spades is one of the two black suits in cards

explanation.surface: Someone is dressed in a dark suit for a solemn occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black suit' looks like clothing but is a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: In spades is an idiom for to a great degree, extremely or emphatically.

clue.text: Schwarzenegger's debut with his familiar name is no classy fare

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so the opening letter of the name is taken

parts.note: Arnie is the nickname of Arnold Schwarzenegger

explanation.surface: The action star's first film, with his nickname on it, is low-budget stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'is' are links. A SARNIE is British slang for a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarnie is a sandwich in casual British slang, humble food rather than haute cuisine.

clue.text: Intimate clothing doesn't breathe quickly enough?

definitions.meaning: underwear worn next to the skin
someone who pants less than enough, a whimsical split of the word

explanation.surface: Lingerie that leaves you short of breath.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as UNDER-PANTS: someone who pants too little.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear worn below the waist is intimate clothing; panting under the mark is breathing too slowly.

clue.text: Isolation as before Kurosawa film projection

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the others in the answer

parts.note: qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of
Ran is a 1985 film by Akira Kurosawa
a tine is a projecting prong

explanation.surface: Solitude before a screening of a Japanese classic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' gives QUA, Latin for 'in the capacity of', a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarantine is a period of enforced separation to stop disease spreading.

clue.text: Acknowledge failings of journal in an assurance

parts.note: an gives the letter A

indicators.note: the journal is placed in the middle of the word for assurance

parts.note: poise is calm assurance
a log is a journal or record

explanation.surface: Someone confidently confesses their faults in a diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To say sorry is to admit one's faults and express regret.

clue.text: Was affected by retreating in battlefield

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the run of letters is read in reverse
in shows the letters sit inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A soldier was shaken by pulling back on the battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: Read battlefield backwards and the letters FELT appear in 'tlef'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have felt something is to have experienced it, been moved by it.

clue.text: Check for presence of jumbo flyer completely crossing lines

indicators.note: the bird's name crosses, or straddles, the lines, holding them inside

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of legend
L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines
all means completely

explanation.surface: An inspection of a jumbo jet as it crosses the lines on a runway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumbo flyer' suggests a jet, but it is the giant mythical bird ROC.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll call is the reading of names to see who is present, a register.

clue.text: Cutler who was entertainingly eccentric cut material for knife handles etc.

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: ivory was traditionally used for knife handles and piano keys

explanation.surface: A knife-maker known for his quirky charm trimmed handle material.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor Cutler was a Scottish poet, humorist and musician known for whimsical performances. 'Cutler' looks like a knife-maker, tying in with the handles.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Cutler was a Scottish humorist famous for surreal, oddball poems and songs.

clue.text: Only one bean to deal with, nothing less, and she lost hers

indicators.note: to deal with things is to sort them out, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone has just one bean to handle, nothing else, and she has lost hers.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of ONLY ONE BEAN, remove an O ('nothing less'), and rearrange. 'hers' is her head: the Tudor queen was beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry VIII's second wife was executed by beheading in 1536.

clue.text: Perhaps nail treatment removing middle part should promote growth

indicators.note: the two central letters are taken out of the treatment's name

parts.note: a manicure is one kind of nail treatment

explanation.surface: Cutting out the cuticle in a nail treatment should help nails grow.
explanation.walkthrough: MANICURE has eight letters; its middle two are I and C. 'should' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To fertilise soil with dung encourages plants to grow.

clue.text: Something catchy that's satisfying — to caterpillar, at least

definitions.text: Something catchy that's satisfying — to caterpillar, at least

parts.note: a hook is something that catches, or a catchy musical phrase
ah is a sigh of satisfaction

explanation.surface: A catchy tune is satisfying, at least to a caterpillar.
explanation.walkthrough: The caterpillar in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland sits on a mushroom smoking a water pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A water pipe smoked for pleasure, as by Lewis Carroll's caterpillar.

clue.text: Temporary release from prison detail?

definitions.meaning: to explain something in full, step by step

explanation.surface: A prisoner's brief parole is described in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a whimsical phrase: a spell, or stint, spent out.
explanation.definitionFit: A stint outside jail is a period out; to explain fully is to set out explicitly.

clue.text: Heading taken from Caribbean pirate's journal

indicators.note: the heading, or first letter, is removed from the pirate's name

parts.note: Henry Morgan was a Welsh privateer in the Caribbean

explanation.surface: A headline is lifted from a buccaneer's logbook.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the M from MORGAN leaves ORGAN. 'pirate's' is possessive, adding no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ is a newspaper or periodical serving as the mouthpiece of a group.

clue.text: Clod from surfaces of brittle rock

indicators.note: the surfaces of each word are its outside letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A lump of earth breaks off brittle rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clod' looks like a lump of soil but means a fool. BERK is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A berk is a stupid person in British slang, a dolt.

clue.text: Grand vessel carrying each pleasure-seeker

parts.note: epic means grand in scale

indicators.note: the vessel carries, or holds, the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A grand ship carries pleasure-seekers on a luxury cruise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship but is an URN.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean is devoted to sensual enjoyment, especially fine food and drink.

clue.text: Grief since confining King George

indicators.note: the word for since confines, or encloses, the royal abbreviation

parts.note: ago means since, in the past
GR is Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: Sadness since King George was imprisoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grief' looks like sorrow but is trouble or hassle; AGGRO is British slang for aggressive trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for hassle or aggravation, close to the informal sense of giving someone grief.

clue.text: We see talk foolishly interrupting thought (and contestants humiliated) in this

indicators.note: the jumbled words interrupt, or break into, the word for thought

parts.note: to think is to have a thought

indicators.note: foolishly means in a silly, disordered way, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Silly chatter cuts across someone's train of thought, and contestants are humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' scrambles the three words and 'interrupting' places them inside the thought. The answer is a British TV quiz show in which players were voted off one by one.
explanation.definitionFit: A TV quiz in which players were dismissed with the catchphrase 'You are the weakest link, goodbye'.
